messages:
evan: Heads-up: onboarding raven-liteq (PTQ-4) in canary. Seeing sporadic omission of the "tools" array during streaming tool-invokes. Small raw-fragment capture below.

marta: Can you paste the chunks?

evan: Here are two consecutive streaming chunks we captured (order preserved):

```
{"type":"chunk","text":"{"call":"c-9","resp":{"ok":true,"tools":[{"id":"t1","name":"save","args":{"path":"/tmp/"}}]}}
"}
```

```
{"type":"chunk","text":"logs.txt","mode":"text"}}]}}
"}
```

evan: If a reassembler glues these incorrectly (cut at tokenizer boundary) our JSON parser sometimes sees tools:null or throws.

yusuf: Metrics? how different vs fp16?

evan: Quick A/B on 2k prompts: fp16 ~0.7% parse failures, PTQ-4 ~3.9%. Retry budget consumed ~1.2% extra on PTQ-4.

marta: We tried sentinel markers (<<<JSON>>>/<<<END>>>). Parse failures drop to ~0.4% but median latency +35ms. Not ideal for p95.

yusuf: Short-term mitigations: (1) length-prefixed ndjson framing at runtime ingress so reassembly doesn't depend on chunk boundaries, (2) on-parse-fail automatic non-streaming retry using cached prompt. Both are low-effort.

evan: I ran a 1k adversarial chunk-split microbench (simulates splits mid-utf8/subtoken). Results: PTQ-4 parse-fail 3.8%, fp16 0.6%, hybrid ~1.4%. Non-streaming fallback reduced visible failures to 0.05% but added median +120ms for retried requests.

qa-bot: CI note: added unit test for chunk-reassembly and a fuzz harness check.

ops-bot: deploy 6500001234 -> canary/raven-liteq: feature flag `streaming_framing=ndjson_lenpref` toggled for test cohort at 14:05 UTC. Monitoring enabled.

marta: Next steps: (a) wire length-prefixed framing in the runtime, (b) add transparent non-streaming fallback on parse error, (c) run full 5k sweep across fp16/ptq4/hybrid with adversarial splits and report back. I'll post numbers in-thread. :thumbsup:
